function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide for pulling *detailed* interface information from a variety of platforms. If you’re working with a specific vendor or OS, let me know and I can drill down further. --- ## 1. CLI (Command‑Line Interface) | Platform | Typical command | What you’ll see | |----------|-----------------|-----------------| | **Cisco IOS / IOS‑XE / IOS‑XR** | `show interface `
`show interface detail` | All counters, MTU, duplex, speed, errors, encapsulation, description, MAC address, etc. | | **Cisco NX‑OS** | `show interface | include all` | Same as above, plus additional NX‑OS‑specific fields. | | **Juniper Junos** | `show interfaces extensive` | Full statistics, link status, MTU, errors, encapsulation, description, MAC, etc. | | **Arista EOS** | `show interface extensive` | Same as Juniper. | | **Linux** | `ip -d link show `
`ethtool -S ` | Driver stats, link state, speed, duplex, MAC, MTU, etc. | | **Windows** | `Get-NetAdapter -Name "" | Format-List *` (PowerShell) | All adapter properties, status, MAC, speed, etc. | > **Tip:** On most platforms you can pipe the output to `more` or `less` to scroll through long lists. --- ## 2. SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) | OID | What it returns | Typical use | |-----|-----------------|-------------| | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1` (`ifIndex`) | Interface index | Enumerate interfaces | | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2` (`ifDescr`) | Interface description | Human‑readable name | | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5` (`ifSpeed`) | Interface speed (bits/sec) | Capacity | | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8` (`ifOperStatus`) | Operational status (up/down) | Link health | | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.14` (`ifInErrors`) | Input errors | Troubleshooting | | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.20` (`ifOutOctets`) | Output octets | Traffic volume | | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.21` (`ifOutUcastPkts`) | Unicast packets out | Traffic type | > **How to use:** > ```bash > snmpwalk -v2c -c public 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1 > ``` > Replace `public` with your community string and `` with the target. --- ## 3. RESTCONF / NETCONF (YANG models) | Platform | Endpoint | Example | |----------|----------|---------| | **Cisco IOS XE** | `/restconf/data/ietf-interfaces:interfaces/interface=` | `GET https:///restconf/data/ietf-interfaces:interfaces/interface=GigabitEthernet0/1` | | **Juniper Junos** | `/restconf/data/juniper-junos:interfaces/interface=` | `GET https:///restconf/data/juniper-junos:interfaces/interface=ge-0/0/1` | | **Arista EOS** | `/restconf/data/ietf-interfaces:interfaces/interface=` | Same as Cisco. | > **Authentication:** Usually Basic Auth or OAuth2. > **Output:** JSON containing all YANG‑defined attributes (status, description, MTU, etc.). --- ## 4. Vendor‑Specific APIs | Vendor | API | What you get | |--------|-----|--------------| | **Cisco DNA Center** | `/dna/intent/api/v1/network-device//interface` | Detailed interface stats, health, and configuration. | | **Arista CloudVision** | `/api/v1/infra/physical-interfaces` | Full inventory and metrics. | | **Juniper Contrail** | `/api/v1/interfaces` | Interface details across fabric. | > These APIs often require OAuth tokens and are documented in the vendor’s developer portal. --- ## 5. Example: Pulling Interface Details on a Cisco IOS Router ```bash # Show basic info show interface GigabitEthernet0/1 # Show extended details (errors, MTU, etc.) show interface GigabitEthernet0/1 detail # Show only the description show interface GigabitEthernet0/1 | include Description # Export to a file show interface GigabitEthernet0/1 detail | redirect tftp:///gig0_1.txt ``` --- ## 6. Example: Using SNMP to Get Interface Speed & Status ```bash snmpget -v2c -c private 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5.1 # ifSpeed for ifIndex 1 snmpget -v2c -c private 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.1 # ifOperStatus for ifIndex 1 ``` --- ## 7. Example: RESTCONF on a Juniper Device ```bash curl -k -u admin:admin \ -H "Accept: application/yang-data+json" \ https:///restconf/data/juniper-junos:interfaces/interface=ge-0/0/1 ``` The JSON will contain fields like: ```json { "name": "ge-0/0/1", "description": "Uplink to core", "enabled": true, "mtu": 1500, "link-status": "up", "statistics": { "in-octets": 123456789, "out-octets": 987654321, ... } } ``` --- ## 8. Quick Checklist for “Detailed” Information 1. **Interface name / ID** – e.g., `GigabitEthernet0/1`, `ge-0/0/1`. 2. **Operational status** – up/down, admin status. 3. **Speed & Duplex** – negotiated speed, duplex mode. 4. **MTU** – maximum transmission unit. 5. **MAC address** – physical address. 6. **Description / Notes** – human‑readable description. 7. **Counters** – in/out octets, packets, errors, discards. 8. **Link type** – Ethernet, fiber, etc. 9. **Configuration** – VLANs, ACLs, QoS, etc. (if applicable). 10. **Health metrics** – temperature, fan status (if available). --- ### Need More Detail? - **Which device/OS are you using?** - **Do you have API access or only CLI/SNMP?** - **Are you looking for real‑time monitoring or a one‑off snapshot?** Let me know, and I can tailor the commands or API calls to your exact environment!
